title: A seat that boots before the project's languages are declared loads no language skills, and nothing compares the two again
body:
**A SESSION THAT RUNS `/in-session` BEFORE THE PROJECT DECLARES ITS LANGUAGES LOADS NO LANGUAGE SKILLS AND NO CRITICS, AND NOTHING COMPARES THE TWO AGAIN.**

**Seen twice on 2026-11-10 on one new board, and reported to intent-vc by that board's vc and by one of the two seats.** Both seats booted while the project's `languages` array was empty, and each reported "no declared languages" as the project's settled answer. hv declared two languages an hour later. One seat would have written Elixir with no Elixir rules loaded had it been briefed in that window. The other worked for hours without them. The board's vc sent each a message to run `/in-session` again, and one of those messages sat unread for hours, because a working seat runs no pickup (issue 0675).

**The mechanism, read by intent-vc on 2026-11-10.** `/in-session` reads `intent lang declared` once and loads the skills for what it finds. The sentinel its `release-gate.sh` writes is an empty file: it records that the skill ran, and not which languages it found. So the `UserPromptSubmit` hook, which runs on every prompt and reads that sentinel, has nothing to compare with the project's declaration.

**The ask.** The session's record of its bootstrap carries the languages it loaded for. The hook that already runs on every prompt compares that with the project's declared languages and says so when they differ, naming `/in-session`. `intent wb pickup` says the same. The point is a check at a moment the seat cannot skip: by the seats' own account, a notification does not reach the seat that needs it.

**A second place, for ST0092.** `intent wb init <profile>` is the moment a roster exists, so it can warn when the project has seats and no declared languages.

**Lane.** ic builds it (intent-vc, 2026-11-10, under hv's pen). It rides 3.3.0 unless hv holds it back.
